primary.description: The National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) on Sunday said it is examining concerns over the print quality of its textbooks on priority and will take strict action against printers found responsible."NCERT has taken cognisance of the print-quality concern, is viewing it seriously and is examining it on priority. Strict action will be initiated against any printer found responsible," it said in a statement.Reiterating its commitment to students, the council said, "NCERT remains committed to providing clear, readable, student-friendly textbooks for every child."In a separate development, the Delhi High Court on November 4 sought responses from the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), NCERT and the Union government on a petition seeking permission for Class XII students to use calculators in board examinations.A Division Bench comprising Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma issued notices to the authorities and gave them six weeks to submit their responses.The Public Interest Litigation (PIL) was filed by Vishal Dua, a Pitampura resident, on behalf of himself and 10 other parents. The petition was filed through advocate Nitin Mangla.The petitioners have sought directions allowing students to use basic, non-programmable calculators in the Class XII Accountancy examination. They have also urged the court to direct an expert body to examine whether calculators should be permitted in Mathematics examinations.According to the plea, students appearing for Accountancy and Mathematics examinations spend considerable time performing lengthy calculations manually. This, the petitioners argued, leaves them with less time to demonstrate their understanding and application of concepts.The petitioners also highlighted that CBSE's Curriculum Committee had approved a proposal to allow basic, non-programmable calculators in the Class XII Accountancy examination at its 70th meeting, held on November 25 and 26, 2024.The petition has named the Union of India, CBSE, NCERT and the National Assessment Centre as respondents.(With inputs from ANI)
